title: About the Network
text:
The Data Donation Network brings together scholars in the field of data donation. It is open to everyone interested in data donation, whatever their location, institution, discipline or career stage.
The network’s main activity is organising the annual Data Donation Symposium. Besides the symposium, it runs communication channels where researchers can share and receive news that may interest their colleagues, such as events, calls for papers and job openings.

Membership
The network has no formal membership. Researchers are free to join the mailing list under their own name and to submit abstracts to the symposia.

title: About the Network
text:
How the network is organised
The network is governed by a Governance Charter. The charter is a practical framework: it does not create a legal entity or any legally binding obligations. The network has three parts:

Steering Committee

Protects the long-term development and continuity of the symposium series. It sets the strategic direction, maintains the network’s identity and communication channels (website, mailing lists), selects future hosts, supports each local organising committee, and supports the Early Career Network.

Local Organising Committee

Changes every year and plans that year’s symposium: logistics, budget and sponsorship, programme, reviewing, local communications, and the post-conference report and handover.

Early Career Network

Connects early-career scholars working on data donation. It nominates representatives to the Steering Committee. More about the Early Career Network →



Steering Committee composition
The Steering Committee consists of up to two people for each previous, current and confirmed future host of the symposium, with one vote per host. A host keeps its seat for five years after its symposium. After that, the seat normally rotates out, and hosting a later symposium renews it. The Early Career Network can nominate two representatives, who together have one vote.
The committee aims to decide by consensus. When consensus can’t be reached, it decides by simple majority of the members taking part.


Selecting future hosts
The Steering Committee selects future hosts well in advance. It considers organisational capacity, scientific fit, geographical balance where appropriate, and the long-term interests of the symposium series.
See People for the current committee members.

title: Data Donation Symposium 2025
text:
About this edition
The symposium brought together applied researchers, methodologists, legal and ethical experts, research engineers and software developers interested in collecting digital trace data through data donation.
Keynote: Philipp Lorenz-Spreen (TU Dresden / Max Planck Institute for Human Development): From DSA Access to Data Donations: Ways to Study Social Media’s Impact on Democracy
The programme had four panels: Tools & Infrastructures for Data Donation, Understanding Participants, Measurement & Empirical Applications, and Survey Design Strategies for Data Donation. It also included a panel discussion with Daniel Angus (QUT), Laura Boeschoten (Utrecht University) and Jakob Ohme (Weizenbaum Institute).

title: Data Donation Symposium 2023
text:
Dates: 11–12 September 2023
Host: University of Zurich
Organised by: Data Donation Lab, University of Zurich
Location: Zurich, Switzerland

title: Data Donation Symposium 2023
text:
About this edition
An international symposium on data donation as a way to collect digital trace data for academic research. It covered legal and ethical aspects, technical and organisational implementation, participant motivation and recruitment, and bias.
Keynote: Paul-Olivier Dehaye (Hestia.ai, PersonalData.io): Beyond data donation – some practical examples
The programme had sessions on empirical studies, legal aspects, bias in data donation studies, data donation collection tools and methodological aspects. It also included a podium discussion on the roles of NGOs, companies and academia, moderated by Thomas Friemel.

title: Early Career Network
text:
The Data Donation Early Career Network is for early-career researchers interested in exchange and networking around data donation. It started as a network of PhD candidates and now welcomes all early-career researchers.
The Early Career Network nominates two representatives to the network’s Steering Committee, so early-career researchers have a voice in how the network develops.

title: Data Donation Symposium 2026
text:
Dates: 1–2 October 2026, with a pre-symposium Data Donation Sprint on 30 September
Host: Weizenbaum Institute (Digital News Dynamics research group)
Venue: Weizenbaum Institute, Hardenbergstraße 32, Berlin

title: Data Donation Symposium 2026
text:
About this edition
The fifth Data Donation Symposium brought together researchers working on the future of data donation research.
Keynote: Jasper Tjaden
Panel: Data Donation, Quo Vadis? The Future of User-Empowered Data Access, with Finn Rübo, Theo Araujo, Lisa Sophie Markschies and LK Seiling, moderated by Jakob Ohme.
The day before the symposium, a one-day hackathon, the Data Donation Sprint, took place at the Weizenbaum Institute. It was co-organised with the Data Donation Lab at the University of Zurich, and the results were presented on the second day of the symposium.

title: Data Donation Symposium 2024
text:
About this edition
The symposium brought together applied researchers, methodologists, legal and ethical experts, research engineers and software developers interested in using digital trace data for research.
Keynote: Melinda Mills (University of Oxford, Leverhulme Centre for Demographic Science): Data4Science
On the morning of 30 May, a short course taught participants how to prepare a data donation study with the Port software. Both the symposium and the short course were free of charge, funded by PDI-SSH and ODISSEI.
